title: Wilderness Medical Society Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Treatment of Acute Altitude Illness: 2024 Update
publisher: Wilderness Medical Society / Wilderness & Environmental Medicine
claims: Travel above 2500 m by unacclimatized lowlanders carries risk of acute mountain sickness (AMS), high-altitude cerebral edema (HACE) and high-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE).
Above 3000 m, sleeping elevation should not increase by more than 500 m per day, with a rest day every 3 to 4 days.
AMS is diagnosed from symptoms and functional status within several hours to 3 days after ascent above 2500 m; HACE is suggested by ataxia and altered mentation.

For suspected HACE, descent is indicated; for HAPE, oxygen should be started if available and clinicians should try to descend at least 1000 m or until symptoms resolve, although patients with supplemental oxygen and adequate monitoring may not need to descend.

For moderate- to high-risk situations, acetazolamide is the preferred prophylactic medication; dexamethasone may be used as an alternative in adults with prior intolerance or allergic reaction to acetazolamide; Table 1 gives specific doses.

verification.note: WMS 2024 高原病指南 PubMed 全文；2026-11-20 将三条概括收窄为原文的人群限定、下降条件与用药优先级。

claimVerification.note: 原文限定“unacclimatized lowlanders”；补回人群限定，避免读成所有人在 2500 m 以上风险相同。

原文：“With travel above 3000 m, individuals should not increase the sleeping elevation by more than 500 m/d and should include a rest day (ie, no ascent to higher sleeping elevation) every 3 to 4 d.” 数值完全一致。

原文：“The diagnosis of AMS is made in a very specific clinical context ... within several hours to 3 d following ascent to high elevations, generally >2500 m. Diagnosis is based solely on reported symptoms ... consider the traveler's well-being and functional status”；“The diagnosis of HACE is heralded by signs of encephalopathy including ataxia ... and altered mentation.” claim 省略了“generally”，属于轻微概括。
原文：HACE 指示下降；HAPE “should try to descend at least 1000 m or until symptoms resolve”，吸氧 “if available”；并明确有吸氧且能充分监测者可能不必下降。
原文：低风险不需预防用药，中高风险应考虑；乙酰唑胺为首选，地塞米松仅用于不能耐受/过敏者替代；Table 1 给剂量。
